correctness.rationale: The four-block Rudin-Shapiro decomposition follows from the signed two-word recurrence. A positioned cyclic 2-Abelian square must have identical first and last symbols in its two halves, excluding all cuts in the opposite-sign blocks and the two quarter-block boundaries. For strict interior cuts in a repeated quarter, both halves share endpoints and exactly one transition at their two changed junctions, while complementing the intervening block preserves its internal transition count. The necessary and sufficient remaining condition is zero signed sum of that block, which holds at precisely odd recursion depths. The zero and lowest-rank cases are explicit. Direct bitwise and recursive independent constructions, followed by full cut enumeration, passed for ranks 2--14 in the embedded checker; infinite validity follows from proof, not the experiment.

value.rationale: The theorem completely determines producing positions rather than a single sample statistic, and shows a sharp even/odd phase transition from zero full-length cyclic 2-Abelian squares to asymptotically one half of all rotations. The problem is a natural higher-order abelian-repetition test on a classical automatic word; the proof explains the parity phenomenon through exact half-block symbol sums and two boundary transitions. Its scope and potential utility are limited to this family and length regime and are not overstated.
